predecessors.name: Later Zhou
predecessors.text: the Later Zhou empire of the north China plain, which Cliopatria's Later Zhou 960 shape and its Northern Song 961 shape draw identically; the southern states were conquered 963-979

successors.name: Mongol Empire
successors.text: the Song remnant on the Guangdong coast and the whole south, taken by Kublai's armies 1235-1279 (the Mongol Empire took the name Yuan in 1271)

capitals.name: Court in exile (Fuzhou, then the Guangdong coast to Yamen)

ledger.x: 960: Zhao Kuangyin founds the Song at Bianjing (Kaifeng).
963: the Song take Jingnan and Hunan.
965: the Song conquer the Later Shu.
971: the Song conquer the Southern Han.
976: the Song absorb the Southern Tang.
978: Wuyue gives up its land.
978: the Qingyuan Circuit gives up its land.
979: the Song take the last of the Ten Kingdoms, the Northern Han.
979: Taizong's army marches on Youzhou and loses 'a crucial pitched battle on the Gaoliang River'; a Song invasion in 986 was again defeated.
1005: the Chanyuan Treaty ends the Song-Liao wars.
1039-1040: Yuanhao attacks.
1044: peace with Western Xia.
1072: Wang Shao takes Hezhou.
1075: Ly Thuong Kiet takes Song land.
1076: a Song army of over 300,000 invades Dai Viet and 'by 1077 nearly reached Thang Long' (as in ngo-dynasty).
1077: peace after the Nhu Nguyet River.
1077: the Song keep Quang Nguyen.
1081: the Song invade the Xia.
October 1081: Li Xian takes Lanzhou in the five-pronged attack of 1081.
1082: Dai Viet gives back Yong, Qin and Lian.
1082: the Song return Quang Nguyen.
April 1085: war ends with Shenzong's death.
1103: the Song annex the Tsongkha kingdom.

1113: the Xia 'took the Qingtang region', but the Tsongkha page has the Song prince Zhao Huaide in 1108 and the Jin ceding the area to the Xia only in 1136; the pages disagree, so the land is not removed from the Song keyframes.
1123: the Jin hand Yanjing and the Sixteen Prefectures to the Song.
1125: the Jin retake the Sixteen Prefectures in their invasion.
November 1125: the Jin invade.
1126: Hebei and Shanxi pass to the Jin.
1126: the Jin hold Hebei and Shanxi; the fighting moves to the Yellow River and Henan.
1127: the Northern Song ends and the Southern Song begins.
9 January 1127: Kaifeng falls.
12 June 1127: Gaozong is enthroned at Yingtianfu (Shangqiu), then moves to Yangzhou in late 1127 or early 1128 and flees south of the Yangtze in 1129.
December 1129: Wuzhu's armies cross the Huai.
1130: the Jin raid ends.
Late 1130: the Song lose the land north of the Qinling-Huai line to the Jin.
November 1133: Qi invades the Song.
1134: Yue Fei retakes Xiangyang.
1134: the Xiangyang front closes with the recapture; Qi was abolished in late 1137.
1138: Lin'an (Hangzhou) is officially declared the capital.
1139: the Jin return Henan and Shaanxi.
1139: the Song regain Henan and Shaanxi.
1140: the Jin retake the plain.
1140: the Jin retake Henan and Shaanxi.
11 October 1142: the Treaty of Shaoxing ends the fighting.
1142: the Song give up the north.
October 1161: Wanyan Liang invades.
1165: peace restored.
1206: the Song go to war with the Jin.
2 November 1208: peace.
February 1235: the Mongol-Song war begins.
1236: Xiangyang capitulates.
1239: the Song retake Xiangyang.
1241: Chengdu falls.
1260: western Sichuan is Mongol in Cliopatria.
1268: the siege of Xiangyang begins.
1273: the Han river bastion falls.
1273: the Xiangyang siege ends; the Yangtze campaign of 1274-1276 follows (Changzhou massacred in 1275).
1276: the court flees south.
February 1276: Lin'an surrenders.
1277: Chongqing falls: 'The strongholds of the Song loyalists fell one by one: Yangzhou in 1276, Chongqing in 1277 and Hezhou in 1279.'
19 March 1279: the Mongol-Song war ends at Yamen.
19 March 1279: the Song end at Yamen.

wars.name: Song conquest of the Ten Kingdoms
wars.outcome: The Song annexed Jingnan and Hunan (963), Later Shu (965), the Southern Han (971), the Southern Tang (975/976), Wuyue (978) and the Northern Han (979).

wars.name: Song-Liao wars
wars.outcome: Song defeats at the Gaoliang River (979) and in the three-pronged invasion of 986; the Liao struck toward Kaifeng in 1004 and the Chanyuan Treaty of January 1005 fixed the border and set a yearly Song tribute.

wars.name: Song-Xia war of 1038-1044
wars.outcome: Xia victories at Sanchuan Pass, Haoshuichuan and Dingchuan; peace in 1044 with the Song recognising the Xia ruler as king and paying 250,000 units of silk, silver and tea yearly.

wars.name: Song-Xia war of 1081-1085
wars.outcome: The five-pronged Song attack took Lanzhou and other towns, then failed at the flooded Yellow River camps (21 December 1081); Yongle fell to the Xia in September 1082; four of six captured towns were returned in April 1085.

wars.name: Song conquest of Tsongkha
wars.outcome: Hezhou and Xizhou taken in 1072; submission of Dongzhan and Mucheng in 1074; Wang Hou's conquest of Tsongkha in 1103; Qingtang renamed Xining; resistance put down in 1104.

wars.name: Ly-Song War
wars.outcome: Ly Thuong Kiet took Qinzhou, Lianzhou and Yongzhou (1075-1076); the Song invasion of 1076-1077 was halted at the Nhu Nguyet River; Yong, Qin and Lian were returned in 1082 and the border fixed in 1084.

wars.name: Jin-Song wars (Jingkang and the Southern Song founding)
wars.outcome: The Jin took Hebei and Shanxi (1126) and Kaifeng (9 January 1127), set up Chu (1127) and Qi (1130-1137), raided the Yangtze delta (December 1129-February 1130); Henan and Shaanxi were returned in 1139 and retaken in 1140; the Treaty of Shaoxing (ratified 11…

wars.name: Jin-Song war of 1161
wars.outcome: Wanyan Liang crossed the Huai on 28 October 1161, lost at Tangdao (16 November) and Caishi (26-27 November) and was murdered on 15 December; peace (Longxing) in 1165.

wars.name: Jin-Song war of 1206-1208
wars.outcome: War declared 14 June 1206; peace signed 2 November 1208 and the Song tribute to the Jin reinstated.

wars.name: Song-Mongol alliance against the Jin
wars.outcome: The Song 'formed an alliance with the Mongols against the Jin' in 1233 and supplied them 'in return for parts of Henan'; the Jin ended on 9 February 1234.

wars.name: Mongol conquest of the Song dynasty
wars.outcome: Chengdu lost 1241; Mongke died at Diaoyu 11 August 1259; Xiangyang besieged 1268-1273; Lin'an surrendered February 1276; Chongqing fell 1277; the last Song fleet was destroyed at Yamen on 19 March 1279.

certainty.note: The unification campaigns and the Liao frontier before Chanyuan are approximate; provincial limits in the south follow prefectures.
The Liao frontier was 'finalized' by the Chanyuan Treaty (1005) and the Vietnamese frontier was fixed in 1084; the Xia, Tibetan and Dali frontiers stay soft.
A moving war front; the pages opened give no line for 1130-1138.
The Huai river and Qinling line set by the Treaty of Shaoxing (1142) was the Jin border until 1234; the frontier with the Dali and Tibetan lands stays soft.
The Mongol war front: Sichuan, the Han river and the Yangtze changed hands year by year.
